minutes.headline: Select Board heard the 30 School Street park workshop and approved the Uma Flowers host agreement and license renewals.
minutes.summary: The board held a workshop with the landscape architect on concepts for the old primary school site at 30 School Street. Board members and residents commented on whether any of the building should be preserved. The board then approved a modified Uma Flowers host community agreement, the 2022 license renewals (KC Sales was held back for a week) and the November 2 minutes. The town manager reported on grants, projects and vacancies. The board also discussed next steps for town offices after the Special Town Meeting.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether preserving the old primary building as a pavilion had been discarded. Urged that the historic preservation district bylaw and community-space needs be seriously explored. Raised Parks Commission involvement.
Asked what makes a park successful at this site. The architect answered programming and activation.

votes.motion: Approve the host community agreement with Uma Flowers Lunenburg LLC as presented with modifications
Approve 2022 alcohol license renewals as presented
Approve 2022 auto dealer and limousine renewals, excluding KC Sales and Service

Approve the two weekday entertainment license renewals

budget_items.what_was_said: The project is complete and was fully paid by the construction grant. The town remains eligible for more funding.
Townsend's withdrawal would raise the FY23 cost for each remaining member.
The basement wiring contract came in at a low price.
The town received a hazmat remediation grant for the old primary school and is waiting on other requests.
The grant covers the remaining Microsoft Office 365 licence costs. A community compact IT grant was not received.
Members discussed the expected town revenue from a percentage of gross sales.

budget_items.topic: Town offices and community center cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A member discussed the cost range for the building options and possible savings from rehabilitating Ritter.

budget_items.topic: Cost of preserving the old primary building
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said preserving part of the building would cost millions.
Payroll, deductions and accounts payable amounts were read for signing.
The library trustees plan a multi-year contract and a raise for the director.
The town manager is awaiting a proposal from a consultant for outreach, procurement and reporting help.

decisions.decision: The Parks Commission appointment ratification was tabled to December 21.
The Ritter shutters and Town Hall chimneys decision was deferred to the 21st, pending input from the preservation district and historical commissions.
KC Sales and Service's license was pulled from the auto dealer motion and will return next week pending a site-plan compliance check.
The senior tax relief committee proposal will go on the agenda for next week. There is no meeting on the 28th.
The TCP building design committee was invited to next week's meeting to discuss modifying its charge.
The public survey on the park site will stay open to the end of the month.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved a modified host community agreement with Uma Flowers Lunenburg LLC.
The board approved 2022 license renewals; KC Sales and Service was pulled from the auto dealer motion pending a site-plan compliance check.
The board held a workshop with the landscape architect on park concepts for the old primary school site at 30 School Street, with public comment on preserving part of the building.
The board discussed next steps for town offices after the Special Town Meeting and reached no resolution; the building design committee was invited back to discuss its charge.
The Ritter shutters and Town Hall chimneys decision was deferred to December 21 pending preservation district and historical commission input.

why_it_matters: The Uma Flowers agreement sets a percentage of gross sales as town revenue, which touches what the town can count on beyond taxes.
The 30 School Street site and the town offices question both turn on whether to preserve old buildings, and the cost of that choice falls on the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: December 21 meeting: the KC Sales and Service license, the Ritter shutters and Town Hall chimneys decision, and the tabled Parks Commission appointment.
Next week's agenda: the senior tax relief committee proposal and the building design committee's charge; the park survey stays open to the end of the month.
